newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty urges release of journalists in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges release of journalists in Belarus.

text.p: Amnesty International on Wednesday called for the release of three Russian journalists who are being held in Belarus accused of illegally filming and crossing the Baltic state's border.
Amnesty said it regarded the three, Pavel Sheremet, Dmitry Zavadsky and Yaroslav Ovchinikov, as "prisoners of conscience" who were being held for carrying out their jobs.

"The circumstances of their detention -- together with previous persecution and attempts by the authorities to prevent Pavel Sheremet from reporting on issues relating to Belarus -- suggest that the three men have been targetted solely because of their journalistic activities," the human rights group said in a statement.
Belarus arrested the team from ORT, Russia's public television station, on Saturday for what it said was illegal filming and crossing of the Belarus-Lithuania border.
The ORT correspondent, Sheremet, had been stripped of his Belarus foreign press accreditation earlier this month.

Amnesty said that two of the three crew members have been officially charged with Article 80 of the Belarus Criminal Code, which makes illegal border-crossing punishable by up to five years in prison.
The arrests have provoked a row with Russia, which has threatened to revise agreements on closer integration with Belarus.
